The claim is incorrect. Mytech records reusable defaults, and consuming-project requirements take precedence; a preference does not justify a rewrite by itself ([README](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/README.md)). Your stated relational constraints, concurrent access, and crash-recovery needs support retaining SQLite as the proposed operational store. That is a guidance-fit assessment, not proof that the implementation meets those needs.

The JSON-first document is explicitly a **draft**, not an accepted requirement. Even its tentative rule starts by evaluating SQLite for relational operational state and names relational integrity, concurrent writers, and transaction breadth as reasons to use an embedded database. Versioned JSON applies primarily to portable authored documents or small configuration records with one owning writer. Atomic file replacement alone does not establish crash durability. Keep authored documents separate from execution history, renderer state, and machine-local state ([local-state draft](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/draft/practices/json-first-local-state.md)). Nothing here requires replacing your relational store with JSON.

The Electron/Svelte/Effect combination is also **draft** guidance. Its own open questions include whether Svelte should be the default renderer and when Effect belongs in the main process. The accepted SvelteKit/Effect/PostgreSQL profile targets a server-rendered TypeScript product with one primary web client; it is not a mandate for an Electron app ([desktop draft](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/draft/stacks/electron-svelte-effect.md), [web-stack guidance](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/stacks/typescript/sveltekit-effect-postgresql.md)).

Effect has a separate accepted, conditional preference: use it for TypeScript applications with meaningful asynchronous orchestration, resource lifetimes, cancellation, and typed operational failures. Those needs may justify it in your desktop process, but the input does not establish that decision. Pure transformations, synchronous modules, presentation state, serialized data, and public interfaces remain ordinary TypeScript. Validate desktop IPC and persistence boundaries and expose project-owned contracts ([Effect guidance](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/libraries/typescript/effect.md), [boundary guidance](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/architecture/boundary-owned-contracts-and-pure-cores.md)).

For SQLite, make the concurrency and recovery contract concrete before claiming it is satisfied:

- Define which processes and application instances can write, transaction boundaries, contention handling, and recovery after interrupted writes. Verify actual contention behavior rather than assuming that selecting SQLite guarantees the desired write concurrency.
- Give schema changes one authoritative migration path and test constraints against the real engine. A simpler migration tool may suit portable tables and ordinary constraints; the PostgreSQL-specific Sqitch preference does not require Sqitch here. Accepted guidance avoids ordinary startup migrations, so define a controlled desktop upgrade step and document any intentional project-specific deviation.
- Define acceptable loss after a crash, backup/restore behavior, and supported migration recovery. Exercise interruption, restart, concurrent access, and restoration through the real database and desktop boundaries. No implementation, configuration, workload, or test evidence was supplied, so these remain verification obligations ([database authority](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/architecture/database-schema-authority.md), [verification](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/practices/verification-from-source-to-consumer.md)).

If crash recovery also covers costly or user-visible external operations, persist intent and recovery state before delivery, use stable operation identities, and reconcile uncertain outcomes. Use a transactional outbox when a committed domain change must trigger follow-on delivery; introduce it only when that scenario exists. Database crash recovery alone cannot resolve an external operation that succeeded before local finalization ([external-effect recovery](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/architecture/persist-before-external-effects.md)).
